title: Hantavirus - Hantavirus
snippet: ## May 2026 Hantavirus Outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) was notified on May 2, 2026, of a possible hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The current outbreak is caused by a type of hantavirus called **Andes virus**. VDH believes the risk of this outbreak to the public is **very low.** Virginians can safely continue with their routine travel as planned. **VDH is closely monitoring and responding to this situation.** To date, one Virginia traveler disembarked the ship before the outbreak was identified. An additional two Virginia residents who sat on an airplane with a symptomatic case-patient but outside the high-risk area are also under public health monitoring, although their exposure is considered to be lower risk. If other exposed Virginia residents return to Virginia, VDH will monitor their health and advise them on public health precautions to protect themselves and others. Information about this outbreak is changing quickly. Andes virus is a type of hantavirus found in South America.

title: 2026 Hantavirus Cases in America
snippet: #### The recent May 2026 outbreak was linked to a cruise ship called the MV Hondius traveling in the Atlantic ocean. Health officials from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the CDC, reported that the outbreak involved the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is known to be more dangerous and can rarely spread from person to person. ### GIS Mapping of Hantavirus Cases in the United States. #### To better understand the geographic distribution of the 2026 hantavirus outbreak, I created a GIS map showing the known cases and monitored individuals across the United States. #### Using the data, I mapped the affected states, including Arizona, California, Georgia, Texas, New Jersey, Virginia, and Nebraska where health officials reported monitoring passengers connected to the MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak. The flow map demonstrates the geographic spread of suspected hantavirus exposures and emphasize the importance of monitoring and tracing cases to better understand potential transmission patterns.

Hantavirus is garnering attention after a rare but high-consequence cluster of cases linked to an outbreak on a cruise ship. What makes this outbreak notable is not the widespread transmission, but its occurrence in an unusual high-mobility setting, far removed from the rural rodent-associated environments where hantavirus is typically encountered. Rodent-to-human transfer is the usual mode of infection. ## What are the symptoms of hantavirus infection? In the western hemisphere, hantavirus infections can lead to hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), which is considered a potentially fatal disease.
